comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C28-C30 regarding brain temperature and LFP measurements. Both evaluations find these control experiments SUPPORTED with solid methodology, confirming no confounding physiological changes from the behavioral paradigm.

Perfect agreement on claims C31-C34 regarding place field stability and remapping. Both evaluations find the spatial firing pattern analysis SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical testing and interpretation consistent with established literature.

Strong agreement on behavioral data (C20-C27, C55-C56). Both evaluations find the quantitative behavioral measurements SUPPORTED with solid methodology. OpenEval additionally addresses C4, C54 which peer review includes in R1.

Strong agreement on SPW-R characterization (C35-C39). Both evaluations find the data SUPPORTED with solid methodology. Both acknowledge the spatial distribution analysis and frequency differences, though OpenEval notes the frequency interpretation remains somewhat speculative.

Divergent evaluations on spatial coding during SPW-Rs (C40-C47). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with comprehensive analysis, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN, suggesting additional analysis needed to fully support conclusions about place cell properties during SPW-Rs.

Agreement on ThermoMaze apparatus design and validation (C13-C19, C73, C3). Both evaluations find the technical specifications and construction SUPPORTED. Peer review additionally includes behavioral claims C4-C5, C54 in this result, while OpenEval addresses these separately.

Agreement on sleep characterization (C48-C49, C53). Both find these basic sleep pattern observations SUPPORTED. However, OpenEval's R7 also addresses C50-C52 about spatial coding persistence, which peer review evaluates separately in R5 as UNCERTAIN.

Agreement on mechanistic interpretations (C68-C70). Both evaluations rate these speculative explanations as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging they represent competing hypotheses requiring further investigation. OpenEval's R8 also includes C57, C63-C67 which peer review addresses in R5.

Divergent evaluations on spatial coding persistence (C50-C52). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED despite smaller sample size, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN, suggesting the evidence for continuity across brain states requires further support.

Partial overlap on claims C57, C66-C67 regarding weakening correlations during sleep. OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to competing mechanistic explanations, while peer review also rates UNCERTAIN, emphasizing need for more in-depth analysis.

OpenEval separately evaluates the ThermoMaze-Morris water maze comparison (C5) as SUPPORTED, while peer review includes this claim within their broader apparatus validation result R1, also rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C1-C2, C8-C11 as SUPPORTED prior knowledge. No corresponding peer review result found, as reviewers focused on novel findings rather than background literature.
